[ASSISTANT_SAID] Fjallraven backpacks are known for their durability and water-resistance.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Before cleaning, check the care label and identify the type of stain.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For small stains, use a clean, damp cloth to blot the area.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For tougher stains, mix a small amount of mild soap with warm water and apply it to the stain.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For stubborn stains, use a paste of baking soda and water, apply it to the stain, let it sit, then rinse.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For tough stains like ink or grease, apply white vinegar directly to the stain.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] If the above methods don't work, try using a stain remover like Shout or OxiClean.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Specific tips for ink stains include using hairspray or nail polish remover.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For grease and oil stains, apply dish soap or laundry detergent directly to the stain.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For mud and dirt stains, let the mud dry completely before brushing it off.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Avoid harsh chemicals like bleach and strong detergents on the Fjallraven backpack.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Fjallraven backpacks should not be machine washed.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Regular maintenance is important to prevent stains from setting in.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended fabric protectors include Nikwax Tech Wash, Granger's Performance Repel, and McNett ReviveX.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended waterproofing sprays include Scotchgard Outdoor Fabric & Upholstery Protector, Kiwi Camp Dry, and Rust-Oleum NeverWet.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] When choosing a product, read the labels, follow instructions, and test a small area first.
